messages:
Sam W: Quick brain-dump: proposing an 'eviction-escrow' layer for prefix demotion. instead of immediately freeing memory we move demoted prefixes into a lightweight escrow for a short TTL so in-flight leases, prefetches, and handoffs can finish without triggering double-fetches or stale reads.
Neha P: interesting. what are the invariants we'd need to keep? how does this interact with lease transfers and prefills?
Sam W: rough invariants: escrowed prefixes are still addressable for reads but treated as lower priority for eviction; ownership transfers can mark escrow entries as 'handed-off' which prevents rehydrate races; escrow entries store only references + small metadata (gen, owner, lease_epoch) to bound mem usage.
Rachel L: can you paste a tiny config sketch? also we should capture the observable signals to measure effectiveness (double-fetch rate, handoff retries, extra mem overhead).
Sam W: sure — config sketch:
```
eviction_escrow:
  enabled: true
  ttl_sec: 30  # default, adaptive under pressure
  max_refs_per_node: 2000
  store_metadata_only: true
  demote_mode: probabilistic  # 0.0-1.0 to tune how many demoted prefixes go to escrow
```
Zhou: main worry is memory blowup if lots of tenants demote simultaneously. what stops an adversarial tenant from parking huge prefix set in escrow and forcing OOM?
Neha P: plan: escrow is capacity-limited and accounted against tenant eviction credits; escrow entries consume 'soft' credits that degrade service if exceeded. also we should allow immediate purge under memory pressure: a short-circuit path that turns escrow into normal eviction by sequence token.
Rachel L: metrics I'd add: `kv.double_fetches{node,tenant}`, `kv.escrow_entries{state}`, and `kv.escrow_ttl_expires_count`. query examples in grafana for the spike.
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout of runtime/eviction-escrow-proto to rc-4 started (build #4821). :rocket:
Zhou: also think about correctness: escrow must preserve read-after-write for a prefix when writes happen concurrently with demote. we should validate by model-checking state transitions (HOT->ESCROW->COLD) and ensure any write bumps generation/token to prevent use-after-free.
Sam W: agreed. implementation sketch: escrow entry holds (prefix_id, gen, owner, lease_epoch, ref_count_hint). on demote we atomically swap cache slot to escrow pointer; readers check pointer and if escrowed will consult owner (or trigger a lightweight rehydrate) but without a full fetch if owner still has data.
Neha P: integration test idea: synthetic multi-tenant fuzz that repeatedly handoffs + demotes + writes, assert no double fetch and no stale read. also measure memory delta under load.
Rachel L: i'll take the spike for the test harness and the grafana dashboards. timeline: short spike this week, repo: https://git.internal/redwood/eviction-escrow-proto.
Sam W: thanks — i'll draft an RFC follow-up with state diagrams and the safety properties Neha mentioned. meeting to align later today 2pm?
Neha P: 2pm works for me.
Zhou: I'll join but would like a specific section on backpressure + immediate purge heuristics.
Sam W: great — tagging the canary.
ops-bot: ci: all unit tests passed for build #4821.
Rachel L: ack, adding acceptance test checklist to the PR.
Sam W: thanks everyone — keeping this short, more in RFC doc soon. :thumbsup:
